dailyInsight.headline: Test whether task-scoped learning stays out of global memory
dailyInsight.insight: Hermes's public source change tells the agent to put task-learned procedures, pitfalls, and task-specific user corrections in the relevant skill, reserving persistent memory for every-session facts. Builders who maintain a source checkout or a comparable learning agent can run a small disposable routing check: give the agent one correction that belongs only to a release-review task, then inspect whether the correction is written to that task's skill rather than promoted into broad user memory.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The fresh commit changes both the prompt builder and memory-tool schema so skills-first routing precedes the global-memory exception. Its regression test checks that this priority is present in the generated guidance, while the new schema names task-specific preferences and corrections as skill material because memory is injected into every future turn.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A correction about one task has a narrow future audience. If an agent stores it as general memory, unrelated sessions inherit a rule they did not earn; if it has a task home, it can remain detailed and useful without becoming background instruction everywhere.

actions.audience: Hermes source-build operators and builders of agents that combine reusable skills with persistent memory
actions.label: Run a disposable scope-routing check
actions.instruction: In a disposable test task, give one correction that is specific to a release-review procedure. Inspect the resulting skill and persistent-memory records. Confirm the correction is scoped to the relevant skill, does not become an every-session directive, and can be revised or removed without touching unrelated work.

receipts.title: Route task-learned knowledge to skills before global memory
receipts.supports: The fresh public change explicitly redirects task-specific procedures, pitfalls, preferences, and corrections to skills and makes every-session memory the narrow exception.

receipts.title: Skills-first memory guidance regression
receipts.supports: The public test verifies that the skills-first routing rule leads the memory exception and includes preferences and corrections in the scoped-learning instruction.

confidence.basis: A fresh public commit, the prompt and memory-tool implementation, and a focused regression test agree on one bounded routing policy that an operator can inspect without relying on activity metrics.

dailyInsight.limitation: These receipts prove intended source guidance and a wording-level regression test. They do not prove how a model behaves in live sessions, that a generated skill is useful, that a user correction is always classified correctly, or that the change is included in a tagged release.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise or withdraw this call if a public runtime test or issue shows task-specific corrections being stored as global memory by default, or if the scoped skill cannot be retrieved and revised for the task that produced it.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for a public release note or runtime trace that demonstrates one real correction being saved, retrieved for a matching task, revised, and kept out of unrelated sessions.
